fixes.title: Alt/az readouts ignore precession - stated positions are up to 1.4 degrees off
fixes.summary: AstronomyCalculations.objectAltAz now precesses (and nutates) the J2000 catalog RA/Dec to the equinox of the requested instant before forming the hour angle - the hour angle is measured from the equinox of DATE. precessFromJ2000ToDate existed with ZERO callers. Verified against an independent IAU-1976 + GMST computation: Vega on 2026-08-03 20:49:14Z from 40N/105W is 6.145/42.90, not the 6.244/43.05 the app stated (which is exactly the unprecessed J2000 answer); a near-zenith Pollux moves 1.33 deg in azimuth because the error is amplified by 1/cos(alt). Every catalog/target caller in the tree goes through objectAltAz, so this is the one seam. Refraction deliberately NOT added: objectAltAz feeds pointing and altitude limits, which are geometric - trueToApparentAltitude is there for callers that want the observed value.
fixes.revert_check: Deleted the `final (raOfDate, decOfDate) = precessFromJ2000ToDate(...)` block in objectAltAz and fed raDeg/decDeg straight to equatorialToHorizontal -> 3 failures ('Expected 6.145, Actual 6.244'). Restored -> 3 pass.
fixes.caveats: The sky RENDERER still projects catalog J2000 positions unprecessed (projection_and_glow.dart, horizon_layers.dart, stellar_objects.dart), so the drawn stars and the drawn grid stay consistent with each other. setViewMode therefore uses the raw transform on purpose - precessing the camera would slide the view ~22 arcmin off the stars it draws. Making the whole renderer epoch-of-date is a much larger change and was not in this finding.

fixes.title: Clicking Capella opens an info popup titled 'HYG118360' while the chart labels the same star 'Capella'
fixes.summary: Two causes, both fixed. (1) The hit test took the strictly nearest catalogue row. HYG carries Capella as two rows 9 arcsec apart - Aa (mag 0.08, 'Capella') and Ab (mag 0.96, no HIP, no name) - which is about ONE PIXEL at a 2-degree field, so the pick was a coin flip between a star and its own companion and the reported magnitude was a magnitude too faint. _resolveCoincidentStar now returns the brightest row within 2 px (below the pointer's own resolution) of the nearest - the row the renderer drew and labelled - and stops merging once the pair is genuinely resolved on screen. (2) HygStarCatalog._nameComponentStars names unnamed secondary components after their primary using HYG's own comp / comp_primary columns ('Capella B'), so no star enters the catalogue, the search list or the popup chip called 'HYG118360'. Nothing is invented: 436 rows are marked as components, and rows whose primary is itself unnamed are left alone.
fixes.revert_check: (1) Replaced `nearestObject = _resolveCoincidentStar(nearestStar, stars, scale);` with `nearestObject = nearestStar;` -> 2 failures, Actual 'Capella B'. (2) Removed the `_nameComponentStars(rows);` call in _loadStarsInIsolate -> failure, the loaded catalogue contains 'HYG118360'. Both restored -> 6 pass.
fixes.caveats: object_info_popup.dart (the cited location) needed no change - it faithfully renders the object it is handed. The verifier's location correction was right.

fixes.title: 'Best Targets Tonight' transit times are computed for the wrong night
fixes.summary: bestTargetsProvider passed astronomical DUSK (a timestamp) as calculateObjectVisibility's `date`, and that scans local noon to the following noon, so wherever dusk falls after local midnight the whole list described the NEXT night - one sidereal day, ~4 min, off every transit. Added AstronomyCalculations.nightDateOf (the date of the night CONTAINING an instant; before local noon that is the previous day) plus a _currentNightDateProvider, and routed the Best Targets list, the sidebar Info tab (selectedObjectVisibilityProvider), the sky planning overlay and both TargetScoringService visibility calls through it. Bigger than the item implied: the same date-vs-instant conflation was live at 4 more call sites inside these two packages, which is exactly why the sidebar contradicted itself about the same object. calculateObjectVisibility's contract is now documented on the method.
fixes.revert_check: Changed ONLY mosaic_targets.dart back to `ref.watch(_currentDateProvider)` -> 'Best Targets and the Info tab agree on which night they describe' fails with Actual 2026-08-04 00:48:52 against Expected 2026-08-03 00:52:48 - the exact 00:48-vs-00:52 slip the finding reported. Restored -> 5 pass.
fixes.caveats: Call sites OUTSIDE my ownership still hand calculateObjectVisibility an instant and have the same latent slip: altitude_chart.dart, target_preview_tooltip.dart, target_queue_panel.dart, sequence_timeline/full_timeline.dart and plan_tonight_sequencer_helper.dart in skotiq_app, and sequence_time_estimator.dart in skotiq_core. nightDateOf makes each a one-line fix.

fixes.title: The Alt/Az view toggle throws away where you were looking and jumps the chart to the zenith
fixes.summary: SkyViewNotifier.setViewMode converted nothing - it only flipped viewMode, and since the two frames keep independent centres the horizontal one still held whatever the last reset parked it at, (az 0, alt 90) = the zenith. It now converts the current view centre between frames with the same transform the renderer uses. `observer` and `instant` are REQUIRED named parameters so no call site can flip the frame without them and silently reintroduce the jump; all 4 production call sites were updated (command_bar x2, view_controls, show_in_sky). A centre below the horizon converts to a negative altitude rather than being clamped up.
fixes.revert_check: Replaced the setViewMode body with the old `if (state.viewMode == mode) return; state = state.copyWith(viewMode: mode);` -> 2 failures, centerAltitude Actual 90.0 (the zenith) against Expected 81.59. Restored -> 3 pass. Making the parameters required also broke 4 existing tests at compile time, which were updated.

fixes.title: The app states three different, all-wrong depths for the bundled star catalog
fixes.summary: One constant now, in a leaf library: packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/catalogs/hyg_depth.dart holds kHygFaintFloorMag = 9.0 (HYG is Hipparcos-derived; counting the shipped 119,626 rows the per-magnitude gain turns over after 9). deep_star_providers re-exports it so the existing HYG/deep-tier merge seam is unchanged; CatalogPackage.complete's starMagnitudeLimit - which feeds the settings 'Depth' chip - was 15.0, the LOADER'S inclusion filter mislabelled as depth, and now quotes the constant; the Deep-Star Tier settings card's hard-coded '~mag 11.5' now quotes it too. The Layers panel already did.
fixes.revert_check: Set CatalogPackage.complete's starMagnitudeLimit back to 15.0 -> 'Expected 9.0, Actual 15.0' (2 failures). Separately restored the card's '~mag 11.5' string -> 'Found 1 widget with text containing ~mag 11.5'. Both restored -> 3 pass.
fixes.caveats: The finding pointed at star_catalog.dart:29 for the '15.0'; that is the loader's default magnitudeLimit and is genuinely a filter, correctly left alone. The 'Depth' chip's real source was CatalogPackage.complete in source_models.dart.
